thread:
maria: Trying to get the quickstart sample app running, but `redwoodctl` login is flaky during onboarding. Followed README on WSL Ubuntu. I ran `redwoodctl init` and created a profile, but `redwoodctl serve --local` fails with 'no active profile found'.

alex: Can you paste the exact commands you ran and the OS? Did `redwoodctl init` actually finish without errors?

maria: WSL Ubuntu 22.04. Steps: `wget .../redwoodctl-linux-amd64.tar.gz` -> extract -> ./redwoodctl init -> chose "Create new profile" -> named it `work`. It printed success. But `redwoodctl list-profiles` shows nothing. Logs show: `open /home/maria/.config/redwoodctl/profiles.json: permission denied`.

sam: That looks like an XDG/HOME permissions mismatch. What does `echo $XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `ls -la ~/.config/redwoodctl` show?

maria: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is empty. `ls -la ~/.config` shows `.config` owned by root (I think I ran an installer with sudo earlier).

alex: Yup — installer run with sudo can create root-owned config dir. Quick workaround: `sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) ~/.config/redwoodctl` then rerun `redwoodctl init --profile work` or `redwoodctl login --profile work`. Also note WSL can map /mnt/c permissions weirdly if you put config there.

maria: Did `chown`. Now `redwoodctl login --profile work` starts device-code flow but then errors: `device code poll timeout` after ~30s. I can't complete login from browser.

sam: Which ctl version are you on? We had a retry bug in older clients where poll timeouts weren't extended on intermittent network errors. `redwoodctl version`

maria: 0.12.1 (installed manually).

alex: We shipped fixes in 0.12.3+ to increase poll timeout and add `--timeout` flag. Recommend upgrading to 0.12.4. For WSL you can use the linux binary tarball: `https://downloads.redwood.ai/ctl/0.12.4/redwoodctl-linux-amd64.tar.gz`.

maria: Can I upgrade via brew on WSL? I originally used the tarball.

alex: Brew under WSL is hit-or-miss. Easiest: download the 0.12.4 tarball, replace binary, `chmod +x`. After upgrading try: `redwoodctl login --profile work --timeout 120s`. If you can't upgrade, manual fallback: open the device-code URL in an external browser and then run `redwoodctl accept --poll-token <token>` (internal helper CLI we use in support).

maria: Upgraded to 0.12.4, retried `redwoodctl login --profile work --timeout 120s` and login succeeded. Thanks. One more thing: the sample app's quickstart still expects a profile named `default` and errors if it's missing. That confused onboarding because init asked me to name the profile `work`.

jim: Good catch. Quickstart should either detect the last-used profile or instruct `redwoodctl init --default`/`REDWOODCTL_PROFILE=work`. Filing a docs/quickstart UX issue.

devex-bot: Opened issue #1453: "quickstart assume default profile causes onboarding friction" assigned to @jim :spiral_note_pad:

alex: I'll update the quickstart to mention `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE` and add a short WSL troubleshooting note about `~/.config` ownership and the `--timeout` flag. Maria — huge thanks for the repro steps, that saved a support ticket. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks all! :heart:
